strongest_angle: Examine how tectonic uplift on the Colorado Plateau forced the San Juan River to carve entrenched meanders 300 million years into southern Utah rock.

key_facts.fact: An astronaut aboard the International Space Station captured photograph ISS075-E-188830 of the San Juan River on October 6, 2026, which was released by NASA Earth Observatory on November 6, 2026.
At Goosenecks State Park in southern Utah, the canyon carved by the San Juan River is about 300 meters deep according to RockGeo and the Utah Geological Survey.
Geologic forces pushed the Colorado Plateau upward starting around 20 million years ago, transforming the San Juan River from a flat plain waterway into an entrenched canyon carver.
